Schedule 1-hour bench plan session next week to agree SLA targets and test plan

header:
Date: 2026-10-21
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Carlos Ortega (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood CSM); Liam Ross, Dr. Anita Patel, Omar Suleiman, Jules Park (Suncrest Bio)
Location: Zoom
summary: POC scoping focused on private networking options (VPC peering vs PrivateLink), region lock/data residency constraints, egress restrictions, workload sizing and benchmark success criteria. Customer wants a short pilot to validate latency SLOs and residency boundaries before procurement approval.
topics: Workload sizing: qps, burst, tokens per request
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we know you all are busy so we want to keep this focused.
[00:08] Liam Ross: Thanks Maya, appreciate it. Quick context: Suncrest is building an LLM-based R&D assistant, must run in our AWS accounts, data can't leave eu-west-1 for patient related stuff.
[00:18] Carlos Ortega: Got it, region lock, eu-west-1. Quick question on scale: what's your expected steady qps and peak?
[00:25] Liam Ross: Steady around 70 qps with spikes to 200 for batch ingest windows, payloads average 1.2KB request, response ~3KB, token sizes vary.
[00:34] Anita Patel: And security wise we need KMS integration, audit logs forwarded to our SIEM, and SOC2 evidence.
[00:41] Jules Park: Also SSO via SAML and RBAC; we want strict tenant isolation.
[00:48] Maya Chen: Perfect — those are standard. For private deployment there are two common patterns: VPC peering and AWS PrivateLink. We should walk tradeoffs.
[00:57] Carlos Ortega: VPC peering gives simpler routing and NT latency a touch lower but requires cross-account peering and route table maintenance. PrivateLink avoids route table changes and is better for strict egress control, but you get an NLB in front and slightly different IP flow.
[01:11] Omar Suleiman: Can you give an order of magnitude for extra latency PrivateLink adds? We care about p95 for short prompts.
[01:18] Carlos Ortega: In our measurements it's typically +2-6 ms depending on region and NAT traversal, but that delta disappears when the overall model compute is larger. For small prompt low-latency workloads it can be noticeable. Caveat: formerly we've seen misreported numbers depending on load and kernel selection.
[01:33] Liam Ross: We care a lot about p95 < 120 ms for our short prompt path. Is that realistic in private mode?
[01:40] Carlos Ortega: With dedicated capacity the runtime + peering tends to hit p50 ~30-40ms and p95 under 120ms for small models; for larger models we need to quantify. We should bench with your actual payloads.
[01:51] Maya Chen: Success criteria proposal: 1) p95 < 120ms for <=512 tokens on 95% of requests, 2) throughputs sustained at 70 qps for 1 hour with <1% error, 3) VPC-routed only, no public egress for sensitive datasets. Thoughts?
[02:05] Anita Patel: That aligns. Also we need proof that audit logs don't leave account and that our KMS keys can be used to encrypt model cache if needed.
[02:14] Maya Chen: We support customer-managed KMS for Private deployments; audit log forwarding is a configuration we can set to your CloudWatch/CloudTrail destination. We'll include docs.
[02:23] Jules Park: What about model artifacts — do they ever land in Redwood-managed storage? We need clear residency guarantees.
[02:30] Carlos Ortega: For Private deployments all model artifacts and cache can stay in your VPC if you choose, we can pin model versions and the runtime will use your storage. In hosted modes artifacts are in Redwood storage.
[02:41] Omar Suleiman: Ok good. On networking: we have strict egress policy so no direct internet out except through our proxy. How does Redwood handle image pulls/OS updates?
[02:50] Maya Chen: Two options: either we run inside your private subnet with a NAT via your outbound proxy or we preload images in an air-gapped repo. For POC easiest is peered and allow specific egress endpoints during setup; long-term we can do a fully air-gapped flow.
[03:05] Liam Ross: Timeline question: how fast can we get a small pilot running? Procurement wants a bench report in 3 weeks.
[03:12] Maya Chen: If we get sample payloads and credentials for a test VPC, we can stand up a single-node dedicated instance in 7-10 business days, run benchmarks, and deliver results within the three-week window.
[03:22] Anita Patel: What about costs for the POC? We need a rough estimate before procurement greenlight.
[03:27] Maya Chen: For a small dedicated pilot with reserved single-node capacity for 2 weeks we can provide a trial pricing estimate; we'll follow up with a formal quote.
[03:34] Omar Suleiman: Benchmark plan specifics? We want to measure cold vs warm latency, KV cache effectiveness, and token throughput.
[03:41] Carlos Ortega: Agreed. Bench plan: 1) baseline single request latencies (cold start measured), 2) warm KV-enabled repeated prompts to show p95 improvement, 3) sustained throughput test at 70 qps and 200 qps bursts, 4) failure injection to validate fallback to hosted variant in case of capacity issues. We'll instrument traces and token counts.
[03:58] Liam Ross: For fallback we prefer deterministic behavior: if dedicated node can't serve, drop to hosted only for non-sensitive shards and failover metrics should be clearly logged.
[04:07] Carlos Ortega: We can configure routing policies and fallbacks per route; we'll capture which requests were routed to which variant in the trace. Small gotcha: logging must be scrubbed of sensitive payloads if you route to hosted.
[04:17] Jules Park: About compliance: do you have SOC 2 docs and ISO certs? We need to pass our internal checklist.
[04:23] Priya Nair: Redwood has SOC2 Type II and we can share the attestation and security whitepaper. For Private deployments, some items are customer-managed.
[04:31] Anita Patel: Can you also show us RBAC controls and SAML setup flows?
[04:36] Maya Chen: Yes, we'll share the SAML guide and an RBAC matrix. For the pilot we'll demo a scoped admin user.
[04:43] Omar Suleiman: A couple of nitty gritty network questions: IP ranges, route table changes, and possible conflicts with our existing CIDR blocks.
[04:50] Carlos Ortega: We'll provide recommended non-overlapping CIDRs; if you need peering we can suggest a built-in mapping. If there's overlap we recommend PrivateLink.
[04:58] Liam Ross: Any latency differences when using a nat gateway vs PrivateLink?
[05:03] Carlos Ortega: NAT adds a little jitter due to SNAT translation but typically negligible compared to model compute; PrivateLink keeps L4 sticky flows and is more predictable.
[05:13] Jules Park: How do you handle log retention policies and where are logs stored? We need retention control and deletion on demand.
[05:20] Maya Chen: For Private we forward logs to your CloudWatch/CloudTrail bucket so you control retention and deletion. We'll document retention options.
[05:28] Liam Ross: Ok, let's map success criteria to explicit bench tests so procurement has clear pass/fail.
[05:34] Carlos Ortega: Sure: Test A - p95 latency for <=512 tokens <120ms. Test B - sustained 70 qps for 60 minutes with error rate <1%. Test C - KV cache activated reduces median latency by >=30% for repeated prompts. Test D - Residency verification: all model storage and logs remain in eu-west-1 and in customer VPC.
[05:53] Anita Patel: Sounds good. What about metrics capture — can you expose per-request trace ids we can ingest into our tracing?
[06:00] Carlos Ortega: Yes we'll add trace header propagation and show examples for Datadog/Jager/OTEL. Some previous customers saw header mangling when proxies mutated SAML headers; we can provide mitigations.
[06:12] Omar Suleiman: For the benchmark harness do you want us to run the load generator from inside our VPC or can Redwood drive it?
[06:18] Maya Chen: Ideally you run the loader inside your VPC to capture real network characteristics. We can also run a Redwood-internal loader to cross-compare.
[06:26] Liam Ross: Ok. On the model side, we want to test a quantized 7B and a 13B-ish model. Can Redwood serve quantized models on Private?
[06:33] Carlos Ortega: Yes, our runtime supports int8/int4 quantized variants; we'll test both to compare latency and token cost. Note: quantization can affect output quality so we'll tie in your eval prompts.
[06:45] Maya Chen: Good point — we should define quality gates. Proposed: perplexity/accuracy threshold on 20 eval prompts, and human spot checks where outputs must not hallucinate patient identifiers.
[06:53] Anita Patel: We'll provide the eval set. Also need to ensure any PHI is redacted in logs.
[06:58] Maya Chen: We'll mark PHI fields and recommend client-side redaction and server-side scrubbing in logs.
[07:07] Liam Ross: Anything else around DNS or service discovery?
[07:11] Carlos Ortega: We use DNS names for endpoints; when peered you can resolve private zone entries we provide. With PrivateLink you get interface endpoints in your subnets.
[07:21] Jules Park: What's the fallback if our CIDR blocks overlap and we can't use PrivateLink in certain subnets?
[07:27] Carlos Ortega: Options: use alternate subnets, NAT through a transit gateway, or a transient peering with address translation. We'll include decision tree in the doc.
[07:36] Maya Chen: Ok, to keep momentum here are immediate deliverables: Maya share network diagram + peering checklist; Carlos share bench script template; Omar provide payloads; Suncrest choose either peering or PrivateLink preference by Friday.
[07:52] Liam Ross: We'll aim to pick by Friday. One more: do you have an SLA or uptime target for pilot?
[07:58] Priya Nair: For pilots we provide best-effort support; for Dedicated customers SLA starts after contract. We'll propose a pilot commitment for a single-node availability of 99% during the bench window.
[08:10] Anita Patel: Ok good. That should be enough for procurement to review.
[08:13] Maya Chen: Great. We'll send the summary and docs after the call. Quick check — any blockers?
[08:18] Omar Suleiman: No blockers, just need the peering checklist and the bench script.
[08:22] Liam Ross: Thanks everyone.
[08:24] Maya Chen: Thanks all — we'll follow up.
[08:30] Speaker 3: [crosstalk] okay bye
notes: Customer requires eu-west-1 residency for sensitive data
Preferred POC timeline: deliver bench report in 3 weeks
Workload: 70 qps steady, 200 qps burst; average payload sizes and tokens provided
